subject: RFI: model immutability & deprecation process clarification
messages:

Cc: procurement@acmepay.com
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: RFI: model immutability & deprecation process clarification

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks again for the RFI packet. A few follow-ups from our security and procurement teams around model lifecycle controls:

1) If a model in your catalog is marked as "pinned" for a customer, is that model considered immutable for the duration of the pin? Specifically, can you describe what changes (if any) Redwood would ever apply to a pinned model (e.g., patching CVEs in runtime, tokenizer updates, parameter re-mapping) without customer approval?

2) What's your formal deprecation process? We want to understand notification windows, migration assistance, and any guaranteed backwards-compatibility behaviors.

3) For models sourced from the open-model ecosystem, can you provide provenance artifacts you supply to customers (model weights checksums, training data manifest, license attestations)? If you provide cryptographic signing of artifacts, please indicate algorithms and where signed material is stored.

We'd like a written response we can include in our procurement binder; a short PDF or spreadsheet is fine. Can you have something to us by end of week?

Best,
Sara
Sara Ng
Senior Procurement Manager
Acme Payments

Sara — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Karthik (SE) for technical provenance details and Neha (Legal) for license/deprecation wording. We'll draft a concise response and attach the provenance artefacts. Expect a formal PDF + a CSV matrix.

Quick answers inline to set expectations:
- Pinned models: we treat a pinned model version as immutable at the model artifact level (weights/checksums). Runtime-level patches (security fixes in the serving runtime) that don't change model outputs may be applied per SLA, but any change to the model artifact or tokenizer requires customer sign-off unless the customer has opt-in to emergency CVE patching.
- Deprecation: standard notification window is 90 days for non-critical deprecations; 180 days when a migration path with automated conversion is provided. We offer assisted rollouts and compatibility tests on customer traffic.
- Provenance: we provide checksums, model card metadata, license matrix, and a provenance bundle (origin URL, training repo reference where available). We also provide signed attestations (RSA-4096) for model bundles on customer request.

Putting this into formal attachments now.

—Evelyn

Eve — draft of the tech section below; feel free to paste into the response PDF. Also attached a short sample provenance bundle (checksums + attestations) and the license_matrix CSV.

TECH RESPONSE (draft):
- Model pin semantics: When a customer pins a model version (catalog entry vX.Y.Z), Redwood guarantees the model artifact (weights.bin, tokenizer.json) will not be changed. The serving runtime may receive non-functional patches (security, telemetry opt-out fixes) that do not alter the deterministic mapping from input tokens to output tokens for the pinned model; such patches are documented in the per-tenant changelog. Any change that affects model outputs (parameter updates, tokenizer normalization, quantization changes that alter probability mass distribution beyond the documented tolerance) requires an approved change request from the customer.

- Emergency patching: In case of critical vulnerabilities that would otherwise expose customer data or execution integrity we will: (1) notify the customer immediately, (2) propose a mitigation which may include temporary traffic routing to a hardened runtime, (3) if no response and risk is high, apply only those runtime-level mitigations that preserve artifact checksums and document all actions.

- Deprecation & migration support: Deprecation notices include: release notes, automated regression tests run against a customer-provided prompt suite, mapping scripts to translate any custom tokenization layers, and a staged rollout plan (canary, 50%, 100%). Default notice window is 90 days; longer windows negotiable in Dedicated/Private contracts.

- Provenance artifacts: per-model model_card.md, weights checksum (SHA-256), tokenizer checksum, origin URL, license file (SPDX where available), and an optional RSA-4096 signed manifest. We store signed manifests in an encrypted object store and provide a signed URL to customers for verification.

Let me know if Neha wants stricter legal phrasing.

-Karthik

From: neha_kapoor@redwood.com <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>

Eve / Karthik — made minor edits for procurement clarity and license caveats. Attached is our "Model Catalog Attestation" PDF and the license summary CSV. Key legal notes to highlight in the response:

- We cannot retroactively change licensing terms for already-released third-party open models; however, we will surface license changes from upstream and provide a migration plan if a license change imposes restrictions.
- The RSA-4096 signature is applied to the packaged bundle (model weights + tokenizer + metadata). Verification steps are provided in the attestation.
- For pinned models, customer-controlled pinning (via config) creates an immutable reference in the customer namespace; Redwood retains the right to apply runtime security patches as noted, but will not alter the signed bundle without express written consent.

Evelyn — ready for you to send. I recommend calling out the 90/180 day windows prominently and attaching the two files.

Thanks,
Neha
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
